judged_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Recording the throttle before retrieval makes a failed fetch's Sidekiq retry silently return success instead of retrying

record.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Recording the throttle before retrieval makes a failed fetch's Sidekiq retry silently return success instead of retrying

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb, the `retrieved_recently?` method sets a Redis key with 60-second expiry BEFORE the actual retrieval happens in `perform_retrieve`. The `retrieve` method calls `retrieved_recently?` first (which sets the throttle), then calls `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error, parsing error), the throttle key is already set, so any Sidekiq retry within 60 seconds will hit `retrieved_recently?` returning true and silently return without actually retrying the fetch. This is a real bug - the throttle should be set AFTER successful retrieval, not before.
